recommendation_summary: Act now: keep the current folder and add a released subfolder that only the three reviewers can write to. A reviewer approves by moving or copying the exact file into it, so the platform logs who did it and when under their own login. Put a seven-year retention policy on that subfolder. Permissions block authors from approving their own work, and a rule or separate check covers reviewers who also author. Rejected: the typed-initials APPROVED column and naming conventions as controls. Asks which platform hosts the folder to scope the setup. Unmet: it never says the platform's approval log is kept for seven years, and nothing stops reviewers from changing or overwriting files already in the released folder.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The customer contract requires each released document to keep its exact approved version, approver identity and approval time for seven years, with no self-approval and no way for later edits to change the approved version. You need this before this week's delivery and want to keep the current folder.
labels.Deleted: A new document system or custom approval tool. A naming convention as a control, because it enforces none of the contract terms.
labels.Bottleneck: Authors can write to everything, so nothing approved can stay fixed.
labels.Checked myself: Only what you told me. I have not seen the folder or the platform it runs on.

note: The plan uses enforceable permissions, but it relies on the platform's who-and-when log without saying that log is kept for seven years, and it leaves released files changeable by reviewers.
